T01.rationale: Founders come from equity options and market making and have run Lyra/Derive since 2021 through two product generations; Derive now earns ~$4.1M annualised revenue, a modest scale.

notes: requires private channel
missing: team size and roles. Public repos show only 2 committers in the 90 days to listing (DRV-23) and the team was reshaped after the failed Synthetix merger (DRV-07); headcount not disclosed.

T04.rationale: In-house design of a portfolio-margin risk engine with public design docs (PMRM, SRM) and repeated Sigma Prime engagements; little public research beyond that.

T05.rationale: No misconduct found in reviewed press, but the team reversed its 'no new tokens' pledge with a 50% mint that critics called a betrayal; regulator and court records were not searched.

T07.rationale: stDRV holders vote on Snapshot (off-chain); execution sits with Foundation and BVI multisigs (3-of-5) whose board can be replaced by token-holder resolution under Cayman law; the 50% mint was proposed by a co-founder and executed by the Foundation.

notes: missing: Foundation/DAO treasury addresses, holdings and spending reports; the proposer could not give a 2025–2029 supply table for the strategic allocation (DRV-08).

T09.rationale: Small early rounds ($3.3M seed 2021, $3M strategic 2022) with backers not identified here; Variant bought in Feb 2026 on undisclosed terms; the team cut ties with investors who backed the Synthetix deal.

P01.rationale: Self-custodial options and perps with paying users: revenue doubled to $1.03M in Feb–Apr 2026 and OI passed $1B in March 2026, though the OI figure is self-reported.

P02.rationale: Options protocol live since 2021; the V2 exchange was audited from 2023 to Mar 2025 and was in production well over 12 months before listing.

P03.rationale: Original sub-account and portfolio-margin risk engine with its own matching contracts, not a fork; no published academic-style research.

P04.rationale: Off-chain matching with on-chain settlement on an OP Stack appchain is a proven pattern; it relies on a semi-permissioned rollup, and audits found 5 critical issues in the liquidation logic, 4 fixed and 1 acknowledged.

P05.rationale: Prices come from the team's own signed feeds (2 required signers in the mainnet config), the chain runs on a semi-permissioned OP Stack sequencer, collateral arrives over bridges from four chains, and DRV supply spans chains via LayerZero.

P08.rationale: Shipped V2, vaults, atomic matching and HYPE markets; the DRV token was promised for Q3/Q4 2024 and launched 15 Jan 2025.

P09.rationale: Settlement and risk contracts are open source with a deployment map; the off-chain matching engine is closed and no reproducible-build check exists.

P10.rationale: Repo design docs explain managers, sub-accounts and assets, and user docs cover token and staking; no public threat model was found.

S02.rationale: All 4 criticals and 2 highs in the Sep 2024 review were resolved, but round-2 critical DRV2-01 (liquidation-bid blocking) was acknowledged and not fixed; no bytecode match to audited commits was published.

notes: metric 'upgrade_timelock_hours' not in evidence pack

upgrade_timelock_hours not established. PMRM_2 is upgradeable and 84 functions are onlyOwner (DRV-23); no timelock contract is in the repo, and the owner address and delay of the deployed contracts could not be read (explorers unreachable). Ask: who owns the core contracts, and what delay applies to upgrades?

S05.rationale: Contracts are owner-controlled (84 onlyOwner functions, upgradeable PMRM_2) and Foundation multisigs are 3-of-5, but signer identities and the owner address of the deployed contracts were not established.

S06.rationale: Despite a 'fixed supply, no new tokens' policy, supply was raised 50% by deploying a new OFT on HyperEVM and linking it through LayerZero; nothing technical stops the Foundation from repeating this after an off-chain vote.

S08.rationale: No exploit found from 2021 to May 2026, and independent press describes a clean track record; absence of incidents is not proof of security.

S09.rationale: Feeds require 2 whitelisted signatures and a heartbeat but are run by the team, with no independent fallback found; the audit noted that oracles using perp prices can be manipulated.

S10.rationale: All collateral is bridged into Derive Chain from Ethereum, Optimism, Arbitrum or Base, HYPE collateral goes through a HyperEVM bridge vault, and DRV supply is cross-chain via LayerZero OFT.

K01.rationale: 35% of revenue funds weekly DRV buybacks, visible as $303k holders revenue in Feb–Apr 2026; staking gives governance only, and bought-back tokens' final use (burn vs treasury) is not stated.

notes: metric 'top10_holder_pct_ex_contracts' not in evidence pack

market_cap_usd and fdv_usd are derived from the last dated pre-listing price ($0.083, 20 May 2026) and CoinGecko circulating supply (999.88M, 21 Mar 2026). No snapshot dated 21–28 May was found, and the price rose after the 26 May listing announcement, so listing-day values were probably higher.

K09.rationale: The 500M mint vests by Foundation policy inside its own Safe, not in public vesting contracts; no supply table was provided, and data providers count the whole 500M as non-circulating.

K10.rationale: 67M DRV airdropped from points with no vesting at the 15 Jan 2025 launch; price fell from the launch-day ATH of $0.228 to $0.0124 by Apr 2025, and no retention data is published.

M10.rationale: On-chain derivatives are in favour and Derive leads on-chain options, but on-chain options remain a niche next to Deribit (Derive ~8% of Deribit daily volume, 0.8% of BTC options OI).

B02.rationale: Revenue is organic trading fees but small and volatile ($133k–$479k a month over Nov 2025–Apr 2026), with growth driven by a few large options flows.

B03.rationale: Buybacks are live and tracked by DefiLlama ($303k of $1.03M revenue in Feb–Apr 2026, ~30%); the rest stays with the protocol.

B09.rationale: Volume leans on a few market makers (FalconX named) and on large block trades such as a single $130M+ structure; no counterparty breakdown was published.

B10.rationale: There is a real fee business (~$4.1M annualised revenue), but the team needed a 500M-token mint to pay contributors and partners, so revenue alone does not fund operations.

C01.rationale: Crypto options are large (~$63B BTC options OI) and growing, but the on-chain slice Derive serves is still small.

notes: metric 'category_share_pct' not in evidence pack

Category share not set: Derive claims a majority of on-chain options OI (DRV-16, self-reported), while independent data puts it at 0.8% of all BTC options OI (DRV-15, Coin Metrics). Neither is a clean category share.

C03.rationale: Revenue doubled quarter on quarter and options volume set records in Feb–Mar 2026 against Deribit; share among on-chain venues was not measured independently.

C04.rationale: Moat rests on market-maker relationships (FalconX, 10+ makers) and portfolio margin, and has not yet been tested by a well-funded on-chain challenger.

C05.rationale: Contracts are open source and forkable; the matching engine and market-maker liquidity are harder to copy.

C06.rationale: Versus Deribit the case is self-custody with portfolio margin; versus on-chain peers the edge is liquidity, which they could match.

C09.rationale: FalconX quoting and HYPE markets are live; the 'major partnership' cited to justify the mint was never named.

C10.rationale: Gives Coinbase users exposure to on-chain options, a sector Coinbase invested in by buying Deribit; DRV is an ERC-20 on Base, Coinbase's own chain.

D10.rationale: Variant bought in, FalconX makes markets and Sigma Prime has audited it repeatedly.

gates.title: Unrestricted mint controlled by a single key
gates.why: Supply can be inflated at will; every other number in the report is conditional on one person's restraint.

gates.title: Sanctions / illicit-finance exposure
gates.why: Listing would create direct regulatory liability for the venue.

gates.title: Core contracts not source-verified
gates.why: Nobody outside the team can see what users are interacting with.

gates.title: Unremediated exploit with user losses
gates.why: Users are owed money; listing would expose new users to the same counterparty.

gates.title: Active enforcement action against the project or founders
gates.why: Outcome could force delisting or freeze assets after listing.

gates.title: Upgradeable contracts with no meaningful timelock
gates.why: Logic can change under users with no time to exit.

gates.title: Extreme holder concentration
gates.why: A handful of wallets can set the price; order books will not absorb their exit.

gates.title: Unlock cliff within 90 days
gates.why: More than a quarter of circulating supply unlocks shortly after a listing window.

gates.title: No independent audit
gates.why: Code holding user funds has never been reviewed by a third party.

gates.title: Material misrepresentation
gates.why: Two or more project claims contradicted by observed data — the reviewer cannot rely on anything self-reported.

gates.title: Security pillar failing
gates.why: Average security score below 1.5/4 — structural rather than one-off weakness.

gates.title: Anonymous team with centralised admin powers
Undisclosed market-maker terms
gates.why: Token loans and call options are where post-listing dumps are engineered.

gates.title: Insider-heavy allocation
gates.why: Team and investors hold more than half of supply.

gates.title: Mercenary TVL
gates.why: Most deposits are paid to be there and will leave when incentives stop.

gates.title: Volume implausible versus depth
gates.why: Daily volume more than 100x the ±2% depth is a common wash-trading signature.
